metadata.title: Suno, Part Two.
metadata.audience: HAI Lyrical Literacy volunteers who have completed Part 1. Internal training, not promotion.
metadata.narration_notes: Host is Rohan V. Full name spoken EXACTLY ONCE, in BOUT. Phonetic spellings are deliberate for Kokoro G2P: 'Rohaan' = Row-Haan. Do NOT 'correct' them. Register is internal volunteer training — never promotional. Pro access was covered once in Part 1 B03 and is not re-sold here. This part is a tour of the ADVANCED TAB, in panel order; prompt-writing craft is compressed into B02 where the Styles box is taught. Create a Voice, the Sounds tab and the Inspo/Audio/Voice attach row are Part 3. Every SunoL2* scene must pass kicker='LYRICAL LITERACY · SUNO TUTORIAL PART 2' to SceneFrame; the kit default still says PART 1. Heteronym pass done: avoid 'separate' (adjective/verb), 'live', 'read', 'close'.

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Rohaan from Humanitarians AI. This is Part 2. In Part 1 you made a song in Simple mode — one box and one button. This video is the Advanced tab: every control Suno gives you, what each one does, and when you actually need it.

show.event: Composer fades up; serif greeting 'Hi, HAI' above it
The ask types itself into the composer
Send arms terracotta; running indicator appears
Three result lines reveal — the three questions the panel answers

props.command: Simple mode only gives me one box. What is in the Advanced tab?
output: Lyrics — what it sings, and how it is sectioned.
Styles — what it sounds like, as comma separated tags.
More Options — six controls, from Exclude to the sliders.

beats.act: Act 1 — executive summary (BLUF): the panel with the lid off
beats.narration_text: Here is the whole idea. Advanced is the same generator with the lid off. Simple hands Suno one sentence and lets it decide the rest. Advanced breaks that into individual controls — what the song sounds like, what it sings, and how strictly it follows you. Nothing here is required. Each control is a decision you take back from the model.

shot.new_visual_element: The whole Advanced panel rendered as a labelled map, sections lighting in turn

show.event: Suno window resolves on Create with the Advanced tab active; whole panel visible
On 'one sentence', the Simple-mode single box ghosts in and collapses
Panel sections rule and label themselves: Lyrics / Styles / More Options / footer
The + Audio / + Voice / + Inspo row above Lyrics is ruled but greyed — named as Part 3
Three questions attach to their sections — sounds like / sings / how strictly
All labels hold: the complete map the rest of the video fills in

props.sparkLine: The same generator, with the lid off.

beats.act: Act 2 — the Lyrics box (top of the panel)
beats.narration_text: The first box is Lyrics — what the song actually says. In Advanced you write it yourself. Mark each section with Verse or Chorus in square brackets, alone on its own line, and Suno treats what follows as that section. There is also a button that drafts lyrics for you if you want a starting point.

shot.new_visual_element: Lyrics box in focus at the top of the panel; structure tags typing onto their own lines

show.event: Lyrics box takes focus at the top of the panel; placeholder 'Start writing lyrics…'
A first lyric line types in
[Verse] types onto its OWN line above it; the bracketed tag pulses
[Chorus] types onto its own line with a lyric beneath
The 'Help me write lyrics' button highlights beneath the box

beats.narration_text: Below it is the Styles box — what the song sounds like, written as comma separated tags rather than a sentence. Name the genre, then the instruments, then the production: acoustic folk, fingerpicked guitar, brushed drums, warm, intimate. Naming instruments moves the result more than the genre word on its own.

shot.new_visual_element: Styles box in focus; tags accumulate as chips, waveform tightening at each layer

show.event: Styles box takes focus below the Lyrics box; empty, placeholder showing
GENRE: 'acoustic folk' types in as a chip; waveform beside it broad and loose
INSTRUMENTS: 'fingerpicked guitar, brushed drums' adds; waveform tightens
PRODUCTION: 'warm, intimate' adds; waveform tightens again
The commas highlight — tags, not prose

beats.act: Act 4 — More Options: Lyrics mode and Exclude styles
beats.narration_text: Open More Options and six more controls appear. The first is a mode switch for the Lyrics box: Write, where you type the words yourself; Prompt, where you describe them and Suno writes them; and Instrumental, for no vocals at all. Next is Exclude styles — the field for anything you do not want in the track.

shot.new_visual_element: More Options expands; the Lyrics mode switch actuates, then Exclude styles takes a tag

show.event: More Options section expands, revealing all six controls in panel order
Lyrics mode switch highlights, active pill on Write
Pill slides to Prompt; the Lyrics box above swaps to a short brief field
Pill slides to Instrumental; the Lyrics box greys out entirely
Exclude styles takes a tag; a matching element drops out of the result waveform

beats.act: Act 5 — More Options: Vocal Gender, Weirdness, Style Influence
beats.narration_text: Vocal Gender picks male or female; leave it untouched and Suno decides. Then two sliders, both starting at fifty percent. Weirdness runs from safe to chaos — how conventional the result is willing to be. Style Influence runs from loose to strong — how literally Suno follows your Styles tags. Raise it when a tag keeps getting ignored.

shot.new_visual_element: Vocal Gender toggles; the two sliders travel their ranges with responding waveforms

show.event: Vocal Gender toggles Male, then Female, then back to untouched
Both sliders shown at their real default — 50% each, magenta handles
Weirdness travels Safe to Chaos; its waveform grows less regular as it climbs
Style Influence travels Loose to Strong; the tag chips tighten their grip
Rule card: raise Style Influence when a tag is being ignored

beats.narration_text: Last in More Options is Duration, sitting on Auto; switch to Custom when you need a specific length. Below More Options, Song Title is optional — leave it blank and Suno names the track. Save to puts the result in a chosen workspace. Create sits pinned at the foot of the panel the whole time. Press it.

shot.new_visual_element: Duration closes out More Options; the footer resolves — Song Title, Save to, Create

show.event: Duration highlights as the last row of More Options, Auto active; Custom reveals a length field
The panel scrolls past More Options to the footer
Song Title field highlights; a title types in, then clears to show it is optional
Save to highlights; the workspace chip resolves
Create — pinned at the panel foot throughout, never scrolling — arms and depresses

beats.act: Act 7 — change one thing at a time
beats.narration_text: You now have a lot of controls, which makes one habit more important, not less. When a track comes back wrong, change one thing and generate again. Change the styles, the sliders and the lyrics all at once, and the result cannot tell you which change did it.

shot.new_visual_element: One description branching into single-variable edits, then the all-at-once counter-example

show.event: Base settings sit at the left with their result, marked not quite right
Three branches draw out, each changing exactly ONE control; changed values highlight terracotta
Counter-example below: everything changed at once, one arrow, one result
That result is labelled honestly — better perhaps, but you cannot say why

beats.narration_text: To review. Styles is what it sounds like, as comma separated tags. Lyrics is what it says — Write, Prompt or Instrumental, with sections in square brackets. More Options holds Exclude styles, Vocal Gender, and the two sliders. Duration, title and workspace sit at the bottom. And change one thing at a time.

show.event: Artifact page resolves on the cream stage
Each line reveals as the voice reaches it

props.artifactHeading: The Advanced tab, top to bottom
artifactLines: Lyrics — what it sings. Sections in [Verse], [Chorus], alone on their line.
Styles — what it sounds like. Comma separated tags: genre, instruments, production.
More Options 1-2 — Lyrics mode (Write / Prompt / Instrumental) · Exclude styles.
More Options 3-5 — Vocal Gender · Weirdness (50%) · Style Influence (50%).
Footer — Song Title (optional) · Save to a workspace · Create.
Change ONE control at a time, or the result teaches you nothing.

beats.narration_text: That is the Advanced tab, end to end. Part 3 covers the features around it — adding your own voice to the mix, the Sounds tab for effects and loops, the Inspo button, and what to do with a track once you have one you like.

The Part 3 question types into the composer
